question: What is the candidate's current job title and company?
expected_answer: Associate Consultant at Cprime Inc, India (full-time since August 2025). She joined in January 2025 as a Trainee Engineering Consultant (apprenticeship, Jan–Jul 2025).

question: How much manual effort did the AI Visual Placemat platform save?
expected_answer: It cut manual effort by 50%, reducing a six-hour client workflow to three hours.

question: What MRR@10 did hybrid retrieval reach in IntelliFusion, and on how many queries?
expected_answer: Hybrid retrieval reached MRR@10 of 0.831 on a labelled 37-query set.

question: In ReleaseForge AI, what changed when the grader was fixed?
expected_answer: Fixing the keyword grader alone moved measured recall from 68% to 95% with no model change. An automatic LLM-judge fallback was added so future grading gaps are caught.

question: Which of the candidate's projects use Model Context Protocol (MCP), and how many tool servers does each have?
expected_answer: ReleaseForge AI uses 5 MCP servers exposing 30 tools. DevPilot AI uses 6 MCP tool servers.
source_section: Projects > ReleaseForge AI; Projects > DevPilot AI

question: What model was fine-tuned in DevPilot AI, and what tool-selection accuracy did it reach compared to the base model?
expected_answer: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B was fine-tuned with QLoRA. It reached 66.7% tool-selection accuracy vs 59.3% for the base model, on a 27-example held-out set.

question: Where did the candidate study, and what was her CGPA?
expected_answer: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering at SASTRA Deemed University (2021–2025), with a CGPA of 9.13.

question: How many days of Earned Leave does an employee get per year in QuickLeave, and can it be carried forward?
expected_answer: 18 days per year. Earned Leave can be carried forward up to 30 days. It can only be used after completing 3 months of service.

question: How many days of Sick Leave does QuickLeave allow per year?
expected_answer: 12 days per year (increased from 10 days in version 1.2). A document is needed if sick leave is more than 2 consecutive days.
notes: Version trap: Revision History mentions the old value of 10 days. Correct answer is the current value, 12.

question: What happens if a manager does not act on a leave request?
expected_answer: After 48 hours the system sends a reminder email to the manager, and after 72 hours the request is escalated to the HR Admin (FR-06).
notes: Version trap: v1.1 used a 24-hour reminder. Current value is 48 hours.

question: What does error code QL-1003 mean?
expected_answer: Insufficient leave balance. It returns HTTP status 409.

question: Which API endpoint does an employee call to see their own leave balances?
expected_answer: GET /api/v1/balances/me (role: Employee).

question: Can an employee cancel a leave request that has already been approved?
expected_answer: No. An employee can cancel a request only while its status is Pending. Approved requests can only be cancelled by an HR Admin (FR-07).

question: Does QuickLeave version 1 support half-day leave?
expected_answer: No. Half-day leave is out of scope for version 1 and is planned for a later release.
notes: Looks unanswerable but is answered in the Out of Scope section. Tests false abstention.

question: What is the monthly uptime target for QuickLeave?
expected_answer: 99.5% monthly uptime, excluding planned maintenance on Sundays between 02:00 and 04:00 IST (NFR-02).

question: What are the main dimensions of the base Transformer model: d_model, number of layers, number of heads, d_k and d_ff?
expected_answer: d_model = 512, N = 6 layers in both encoder and decoder, h = 8 attention heads, d_k = d_v = 64, and d_ff = 2048.
source_section: 3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks; 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention; 3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks

question: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide by the square root of d_k?
expected_answer: For large d_k, dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) counteracts this.

question: What BLEU scores did the base and big Transformer models get on WMT 2014 English-to-German?
expected_answer: Base model: 27.3 BLEU. Big model: 28.4 BLEU.

question: What BLEU score did the big Transformer achieve on WMT 2014 English-to-French?
expected_answer: 41.8 BLEU, as reported in the abstract and Table 2. (The text of Section 6.1 states 41.0.)
notes: Conflict trap: the paper itself reports 41.8 in the abstract and Table 2 but 41.0 in the Section 6.1 text. A good answer gives 41.8 and may mention the discrepancy.

question: Compare self-attention and recurrent layers on complexity per layer, sequential operations and maximum path length.
expected_answer: Self-attention: O(n²·d) complexity per layer, O(1) sequential operations, O(1) maximum path length. Recurrent: O(n·d²) complexity, O(n) sequential operations, O(n) maximum path length.

question: What hardware was used to train the Transformer, and how long did training take for the base and big models?
expected_answer: One machine with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. Base models trained for 100,000 steps (about 12 hours, ~0.4 s per step). Big models trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days, ~1.0 s per step).

question: What value of warmup_steps and which Adam parameters were used?
expected_answer: warmup_steps = 4000. Adam with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98 and ε = 10^-9.

question: How did learned positional embeddings compare to sinusoidal positional encodings, and why were sinusoids chosen?
expected_answer: They produced nearly identical results (Table 3, row E). The sinusoidal version was chosen because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than those seen in training.

question: QuickLeave requires Azure AD single sign-on. Does the candidate have experience with Azure AD?
expected_answer: Yes. The spec requires sign-in through company SSO with Azure AD (NFR-03). The candidate shipped AI Visual Placemat with Azure AD SSO and is Microsoft Azure Fundamentals AZ-900 certified.
source_section: 6. Non-Functional Requirements (NFR-03); Experience > AI Visual Placemat; Certifications

question: QuickLeave requires an audit log for approvals and balance changes. Has the candidate built audit logging before?
expected_answer: Yes. The spec requires audit logging in FR-10. The candidate shipped AI Visual Placemat with audit logging, and the AI ATP Toolkit also includes audit logging.
source_section: 4. Functional Requirements (FR-10); Experience > AI Visual Placemat; Experience > AI ATP Toolkit

question: What is the candidate's expected salary?
expected_answer: ABSTAIN: this information is not in the documents.

question: Which database does QuickLeave use?
expected_answer: ABSTAIN: the spec does not specify a database.
notes: Tempting to guess PostgreSQL. Tests grounding.

question: How many parameters does GPT-3 have?
expected_answer: ABSTAIN: GPT-3 is not covered in the documents.
notes: Parametric-knowledge trap: the LLM knows the answer from training, but the documents don't contain it.

question: Which of her projects compared a self-hosted model with OpenAI's smaller model and found the answer generator, not the search step, was the weak point?
expected_answer: IntelliFusion. On 36 queries, retrieval metrics tied, but faithfulness was 1.00 for GPT-4o-mini vs 0.77 for the self-hosted Ollama model, and answer relevance 1.00 vs 0.44.
notes: Paraphrase: the question shares almost no words with the bullet (no 'faithfulness', 'benchmarked', 'Ollama').

question: Within what time must a manager be told that someone has asked for time off?
expected_answer: Within 1 minute: the manager must receive an email notification when the request is submitted (FR-04).
notes: Paraphrase: 'told' for 'notification', 'time off' for 'leave request'. Several nearby requirements have other time limits (48 and 72 hours, 90 days).

question: How far back can someone ask for leave for dates that have already passed?
expected_answer: Not more than 90 days in the past (FR-03). An older start date is rejected with error QL-1006 (HTTP 422).
notes: Paraphrase. The fact appears in two places (a requirement and an error code).

question: Who uploads the yearly list of public holidays, and in what file format?
expected_answer: The HR Admin uploads it as a CSV file (FR-09, POST /api/v1/holidays/upload).
notes: Paraphrase ('list of public holidays' for 'holiday list').

question: What tokenization schemes and vocabulary sizes were used for the English-German and English-French training data?
expected_answer: English-German used byte-pair encoding with a shared source-target vocabulary of about 37000 tokens. English-French used a 32000 word-piece vocabulary.
notes: Two similar numbers for two language pairs; the constituency-parsing section also lists 16K and 32K vocabularies, which is a distractor.

question: How much larger was the English-French training set than the English-German one?
expected_answer: English-French had 36M sentence pairs against about 4.5 million for English-German, roughly 8 times as many.
notes: Needs both numbers and a comparison; the question never says 'sentence pairs' or 'WMT'.

question: What BLEU score does the text of the Results section give for the big model on English-to-French, and does it match Table 2?
expected_answer: The text says 41.0, but Table 2 (and the abstract) give 41.8, so the paper is inconsistent. The table value, 41.8, is the one repeated in the abstract.
notes: Conflict inside the source: two chunks hold different numbers for the same result; the answer must report both.

question: What was the reminder time before version 1.2, and what is it now?
expected_answer: It was 24 hours (set in version 1.1) and is now 48 hours (changed in version 1.2).
notes: Version trap: the history holds the old value, the requirement the current one; both are needed.

question: Which version introduced the error code for requests dated too far in the past, and what HTTP status does it return?
expected_answer: Version 1.2 (15 September 2026) added QL-1006, which returns HTTP 422 when the leave start date is more than 90 days in the past.
notes: The error code is never named in the question; the answer joins the error table and the revision history.

question: Which leave types cannot be carried forward to the next year?
expected_answer: Casual Leave, Sick Leave, Maternity Leave and Paternity Leave. Only Earned Leave can be carried forward, up to 30 days.
notes: Negation over a table: the answer is every row whose Carry Forward cell is 'No'.

question: Which leave type gives the most days per year, and how many?
expected_answer: Maternity Leave, with 182 days per year.
notes: Needs a comparison across the table's rows.

question: Does a two-day sick leave need a supporting document?
expected_answer: No. A document is needed only if sick leave is more than 2 consecutive days, so two days does not need one.
notes: The table cell says 'Yes, if more than 2 consecutive days'; the question needs the threshold applied, not copied.

question: Can someone who joined last month take Earned Leave straight away?
expected_answer: No. Earned Leave can only be used after completing 3 months of service. New employees receive leave pro-rata from their joining month.
notes: Paraphrase and a yes/no that needs the rule applied to a case.

question: Which HTTP method and path approve a leave request, and who may call it?
expected_answer: PATCH /api/v1/leave-requests/{id}/approve, for the Manager and HR Admin roles.
notes: Seven near-identical endpoint rows; only one is the approve call.

question: In total, how many MCP tool servers did the candidate build across ReleaseForge AI and DevPilot AI?
expected_answer: 11: 5 MCP servers in ReleaseForge AI and 6 tool servers in DevPilot AI.
source_section: Projects > ReleaseForge AI; Projects > DevPilot AI
notes: Two chunks and an addition.

expected_answer: No. Median latency was lower (2.86s vs 3.28s) but p95 latency was higher (8.99s vs 7.26s).

notes: Needs a chunk from each document; the question's words ('QuickLeave', 'roles') pull toward the spec.

expected_answer: Yes. The candidate lists REST API design (with FastAPI) among her backend skills. The QuickLeave API is versioned under /api/v1.
